scenario: Elderly man with right knee osteoarthritis and a possibly swollen painful left calf; ultrasound for clot.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Namaste uncle, please come in and sit. Be careful with the step.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Namaste doctor. Thank you. My son dropped me, he is parking the car. The parking here is always so full.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: No problem. What is troubling you?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: The right knee, doctor. It has been paining a lot, especially on the stairs and when I get up from the chair.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: For how long?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: On and off for two years. But the last two weeks it is more, I think. Maybe fifteen days, maybe more.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any swelling, redness, or fever?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: A little swelling in the evening. No redness, no fever. And the knee does not lock.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any other joint pain? Any injury or fall?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Both hands are stiff in the morning, a little. No fall. But after the bus journey to my village last week, my left calf was also paining and looked a bit swollen. I am not sure which day it started.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hmm, I will look at that. What medicines are you taking?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Telmisartan for the pressure, forty milligrams. And diclofenac tablet from the chemist whenever the knee is bad, almost daily now. Sometimes paracetamol also.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any allergy to any medicine?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Never had any allergy to any medicine, doctor.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good. Any past illnesses? Any family history of joint problems?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Pressure for fifteen years. Sugar borderline. My mother also had bad knees, she used a stick.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me check. Your blood pressure is 138 over 84 and pulse is 76. The right knee has mild swelling and crepitus, that grating feeling, and tenderness along the inner side. Movement is painful at the end of bending. The knee is not hot.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, what about my calf? Is it dangerous? My friend had a clot in his leg after a flight and he was in the ICU.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: The left calf is a little tender and slightly swollen compared to the right one. I hope it is not dangerous, but a clot is possible, so I want an ultrasound of the leg veins today, before you go home. The knee itself is osteoarthritis, the wear and tear type, which is very common at your age.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And for the knee, do I need any tests?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: We will do an x-ray of both knees, and a blood test for uric acid and vitamin D.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And the diclofenac tablets?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Please stop the diclofenac tablets, they are not good with your pressure and your stomach. Use paracetamol 650 milligrams, up to three times a day, and diclofenac gel on the knee. I will also give you calcium with vitamin D once a day.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. And exercise?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, gentle exercises for the thigh muscles, and lose a little weight. Avoid sitting on the floor, and avoid too many stairs. Come back in a week with the ultrasound and x-ray reports.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Thank you, doctor.

gold.key: a little swelling in the evening
hands are stiff in the morning
left calf is a little tender
gentle exercises for the thigh muscles

notes: Elderly speaker, so slower, more hedged speech. Parking small talk in turns 0 to 2 is unlabelled. Turn 5 has a long, clear duration (two years) and a hedged recent worsening (the last two weeks, I think; maybe fifteen days, maybe more). Turn 9 contains a possible red flag for deep vein thrombosis (left calf pain and swelling after a long bus journey, hedged by not being sure which day), labelled red_flag with uncertain true, while no fall and the stiff hands are labelled as ordinary symptoms. Turn 15 sugar borderline is a hedged history item. The friend's clot in turn 17 is anecdote and is not labelled as history. The patient takes telmisartan, diclofenac tablets and paracetamol; the doctor stops diclofenac tablets (plan), advises diclofenac gel (a different formulation of the same drug), paracetamol, and adds calcium with vitamin D.
